topology.logical_database_isolation: one local Turso Database file owned by one Native runtime process per Native logical database

operational_identity.write_authority: A successful local Turso Database transaction commit in the single owning Native runtime is authoritative; no remote acknowledgement exists.
operational_identity.consistency: Local transaction visibility only. Intra-process concurrent tasks require operation-level proof; multi-process writers are unsupported.
operational_identity.file_semantics: The local Turso Database file is authoritative for this profile. SQLite dialect and compatibility do not make it a stock SQLite ownership artifact; only a quiesced unencrypted file may be treated as a convertible fast path after canonical verification.
promotion_rules: Vendor beta or production claims are not Native support evidence.
A supported revision must use a stable non-prerelease turso crate and pin its exact qualified engine and driver range.
Promotion requires the full Native logical, physical, operational, migration, backup, restore, and recovery suites for this exact topology.
Any engine, driver, connection-mode, topology, write-authority, consistency, or file-semantics change creates a new immutable profile revision.

native.domain-mcp.v1.contract: bounded Turso EngineHandle lifecycle, attachment/blob, link, visibility, authorized history, event-chain replay, guarded-write, request-wrapper, logical-database isolation, live structured query and rollup evaluation, and non-lexical scan slice
native.domain-mcp.v1.notes: No revision 1 or prerelease-driver evidence is inherited. The turso-local feature uses the shared backend-neutral domain transaction seam for the exact operations classified partial in backend-contract-classifications.json. query_record excludes historical projection, activity terminals, interpretation and federated-Message provenance enrichment, and governed comments; resolve_rollup excludes revision receipts plus revision-keyed caching and fencing; scan excludes its lexical axis. The profile remains a spike and does not imply migration, backup/recovery, lexical search, cloud, sync, or operational support qualification.

native.operation.record-read.v1.notes: Historical and enrichment selector parity is not proven.

native.operation.record-history.v1.notes: Global history, run/order selectors, and every caller mode are not proven.

native.operation.snapshot-export.v1.notes: A physical file round-trip probe is not an export_snapshot runtime operation. No Turso-local snapshot handler or canonical verification path is implemented.

native.interaction-log.v1.notes: The deterministic Turso harness does not materialize SQLite read_log_calls/read_log_touches; the optional tap is not runtime evidence.

native.guarded-write.v1.provider: deterministic harness admission gate plus Turso IMMEDIATE transaction and digest re-check

native.search.lexical.v1.provider: Turso FTS (Tantivy) probe; Native ranking adapter not implemented

native.search.semantic.v1.notes: The embedding write seam is dormant and no semantic query adapter ships yet.

native.search.sqlite-fts5-exact.notes: Turso FTS is not SQLite FTS3/4/5.

native.raw-sql.provider: Exact-parser-qualified SELECTs over a fresh caller-visible Turso core MemoryIO projection with no authoritative database path, ATTACH capability, or source-file access; core query-only, progress, deadline, interrupt, and bounded-result controls are mandatory
native.raw-sql.notes: query_sql never executes caller SQL against the authoritative Turso-local file; Native materializes only the authorized ten-relation logical projection and rejects atomically at source, projection, execution, or result limits.

native.describe-physical-schema.provider: Runtime-owned canonical DDL with an exact ordinary value_num column maintained atomically by the shared projector, exact Turso FTS index definitions, and fail-closed schema/seed validation

native.sqlite-file-fast-path.notes: A quiesced, local, unencrypted file round-trips with stock SQLite; canonical verification is still mandatory.
